# Ray Tracing and Ray Intersection Methods

Also called: Ray Casting, Ray-Surface Intersection, Analytical Ray Intersection

## Overview
Ray tracing determines the color of a pixel by computing the distance to the first object intersected by a camera ray in the 3D world [S1, unofficial]. It solves the problem of visibility and shading by finding the closest intersection point along the ray's path. Unlike ray-marching, which approximates intersections via fixed steps, ray tracing analytically computes intersection distances for simple geometries, offering higher precision and efficiency when the geometry allows [S1, unofficial]. It differs from [Ray-box intersection](776-ray-box-intersection.md) and [Ray-Tetrahedron Intersection](2525-ray-tetrahedron-intersection.md) by encompassing the broader class of intersection tests for various primitives, while [Hybrid Implicit Isosurface Ray Tracing](3832-hybrid-implicit-isosurface-ray-tracing.md) combines these analytical tests with hierarchical acceleration structures for volume data.

## Shared principles
The shared principles of this family are the geometric definition of rays and the parallel execution model.

**Ray Definition**
Rays are defined by an origin $\mathbf{o}$ and a direction $\mathbf{d}$. The direction is typically normalized. The origin is often the camera eye position, but can vary based on the camera model.

**Parallel Execution**
Computations are mapped to parallel threads. Each thread typically processes one or more pixels or samples. Memory access patterns are optimized for coalescing. Synchronization is used to manage data dependencies between threads.

## Subtopics

### [Binary Search IsoSurface Extraction](1316-binary-search-isosurface-extraction.md)
Approximates isosurface position via iterative bisection. Choose when analytical solutions are unstable or when working with discrete texture samples.

### [Trilinear Isosurface Intersection](2213-trilinear-isosurface-intersection.md)
Analytically solves for intersections with trilinearly interpolated grids. Choose for high-precision surface extraction in regular grids.

### [Hybrid Implicit Isosurface Ray Tracing](3832-hybrid-implicit-isosurface-ray-tracing.md)
Combines BVH acceleration with implicit voxel intersection. Choose for large, sparse, or rectilinear volumes where explicit polygon extraction is costly.

### [Neubauer Iso-surface Ray Casting](7024-neubauer-iso-surface-ray-casting.md)
Uses spatial subdivision and projection-based culling. Choose for real-time rendering on multi-core CPUs where hierarchical pruning is beneficial.

### [Ray-box intersection](776-ray-box-intersection.md)
Tests intersection with axis-aligned or oriented bounding boxes. Choose for broad-phase collision detection or acceleration structure traversal.

### [General Ray-Triangle Intersection (Plücker Coordinates)](909-general-ray-triangle-intersection-pl-cker-coordinates.md)
Uses Plücker coordinates for robust triangle intersection. Choose for polygonal mesh rendering.

### [Ray Crossing Count (Winding Number)](915-ray-crossing-count-winding-number.md)
Determines inside/outside status by counting ray crossings. Choose for complex non-manifold or closed surface containment tests.

### [Sphere Intersection](1620-sphere-intersection.md)
Analytical intersection with spheres. Choose for simple primitives or particle systems.

### [Ray-Volume Intersection (Face Distance Method)](2381-ray-volume-intersection-face-distance-method.md)
Computes entry/exit distances for volume traversal. Choose for volumetric rendering stepping.

### [Ray-Tetrahedron Intersection](2525-ray-tetrahedron-intersection.md)
Intersection with tetrahedral elements. Choose for unstructured grid volume rendering.

### [Point-Triangle Distance](2776-point-triangle-distance.md)
Computes distance from point to triangle. Choose for proximity queries or soft shadows.

### [Implicit Surface and SDF Intersection](2795-implicit-surface-and-sdf-intersection.md)
Intersects with Signed Distance Functions. Choose for smooth, procedural, or CSG-based geometry.

### [Exact Rational Ray-Surfel Evaluation](2915-exact-rational-ray-surfel-evaluation.md)
Uses exact arithmetic for robust intersection. Choose when numerical stability is critical.

### [LinPrim Gradient Computation](3038-linprim-gradient-computation.md)
Computes gradients for linear primitives. Choose for shading and normal estimation.

### [Ray ID Caching](3110-ray-id-caching.md)
Caches ray identifiers for coherence. Choose for coherent ray tracing scenarios.

### [IRIS Ray-Geometry Intersection](3250-iris-ray-geometry-intersection.md)
Specific intersection routine for IRIS systems. Choose for legacy or specific hardware implementations.

### [Ray-Sphere Intersection](3539-ray-sphere-intersection.md)
Standard sphere intersection. Choose for basic primitive testing.

### [Ray-Object Intersection Test](3604-ray-object-intersection-test.md)
Generic object intersection interface. Choose for abstracting primitive types.

### [Azimuthal Hit Detection](3885-azimuthal-hit-detection.md)
Detects hits based on azimuthal angles. Choose for cylindrical or spherical coordinate systems.

### [Ray-Polar Section Intersection](3886-ray-polar-section-intersection.md)
Intersects with polar sections. Choose for polar-coordinate-based geometry.

### [Ray-Cylinder Intersection](5014-ray-cylinder-intersection.md)
Analytical intersection with cylinders. Choose for cylindrical primitives.

### [Point-Plane Reflection](5920-point-plane-reflection.md)
Reflects points across planes. Choose for mirror reflections or planar projections.

### [Ray-Primitive and Segment Intersection](6230-ray-primitive-and-segment-intersection.md)
Intersects rays with line segments. Choose for edge-based geometry or skeletal structures.

### [Ray-Plane/Rectangle Intersection](6498-ray-plane-rectangle-intersection.md)
Intersects with planes or rectangles. Choose for planar surfaces or clipping planes.

### [Ray-Ray Intersection](7624-ray-ray-intersection.md)
Finds intersection between two rays. Choose for ray-casting against other rays or light paths.

### [Ray-Splat/Gaussian Intersection](7916-ray-splat-gaussian-intersection.md)
Intersects with Gaussian splats. Choose for novel view synthesis or point-based rendering.

### Packet Ray List Merging
Packet Ray List Merging is an optimization where lists of adjacent pixels (typically 2x2 groups) are combined into a single list [S2, unofficial]. It exploits spatial coherence where adjacent pixels share common visible blocks, reducing the number of lists generated and processed [S2, unofficial]. In Phase I, the BONO tree is traversed, and lists are created for each packet of rays rather than individual pixels [S2, unofficial]. If a group of pixels overlaps with the projection of the current node, the group's list is processed [S2, unofficial]. The upper bound $k$ on the list size is increased compared to single pixels; best performance is achieved when $k$ is around 20 for packets, compared to 12 for single pixels [S2, unofficial].

### Hybrid Packetization Strategy
Hybrid Packetization Strategy is a ray-triangle intersection strategy that switches between standard warp-level intersection and parallel processing based on workload [S3, unofficial]. It optimizes for specific GPU architectures (e.g., Fermi) by distributing work for a single ray to many threads to speed up traversal and improve SIMD utilization [S3, unofficial].

## Background
Ray tracing was introduced as a surface rendering technique to determine which object a ray intersects first [S1, unofficial]. The goal is to compute the distance between the camera and the intersection point for each object to find the first intersection [S1, unofficial]. It is one of the most efficient techniques when object geometry is simple enough for analytical computation [S1, unofficial]. When geometry is too complex for analytical solutions, ray-marching is used instead, marching along the ray by a fixed step size [S1, unofficial]. Sphere-marching is an optimized cousin of ray-marching that uses Signed Distance Functions (SDFs) [S1, unofficial]. The method fails when object geometry is too complex for analytical intersection solutions [S1, unofficial].
